subject: SignalPay onboarding: SDK init, endpoint migration & throttle guidance
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <dev+eng@signalpay.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rita Gomez <ops@signalpay.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding kickoff + SDK setup questions

Hi Markus —

Thanks for taking this. We're gearing up to migrate two production endpoints from our in-house gateway to Redwood's hosted runtime next month (checkout and fraud endpoints). Attached is a short requirements doc and an initial SOW. High level asks:

- Quick SDK setup for Node and Python (we'll start with Node for checkout).
- Migration plan for endpoint cutover with a brief rollback plan.
- Recommended retry/backoff and timeout values for high-throughput payment flows (sensitive to latency).
- Rate-limit handling guidance (we expect bursts during peak traffic windows).

Can we sync today or tomorrow for a 30-min bootcamp? Preferably someone who can walk our engineers through code samples and environment variables.

Thanks —
Daniel
Sr. Platform Engineer, SignalPay
Attachments: signalpay_mrp_requirements.pdf, sow-draft.docx

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <dev+eng@signalpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding kickoff + SDK setup questions

Hi Daniel —

Great to meet you (virtually). Monica will lead the formal onboarding; I'll run the technical bootcamp with Grace and Vanessa on the call. Quick responses below and a short action plan.

Action items (short):
- We can run a 30-min "Bootcamp + Hands-on" tomorrow 10:00 PT — Monica, please confirm.
- I'll attach a small sample bundle (Node + Python) to this thread after the call.
- Migration approach: shadow traffic -> canary (10%) -> ramp (50%) -> cutover. Rollback = revert routing + keep old gateway warm for 15 min.

Immediate recommendations (first-pass):
- SDK init (Node): include connection pooling and token rotation. Example snippet: 

  // Node example (redwood-js)
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/runtime');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({
    apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY,
    region: 'us-west-2',
    maxConnections: 50, // pool size tuned to instance vCPU
    defaultTimeoutMs: 2000 // conservative default for payment flow
  });

- Retry/backoff policy (recommended):
  - Idempotent calls: up to 5 attempts, exponential backoff starting at 100ms, cap 2s.
  - Non-idempotent: 1 retry only, use server-side idempotency keys.
  - Circuit-breaker: trip after 5 failed attempts within 30s for a given host, cooldown 60s.

- Timeouts:
  - Client socket timeout = 3s
  - Application-level per-token timeout for streaming = 1500ms

- Rate limits: adopt a hybrid approach: local leaky-bucket client + server-side quota awareness. Return 429 handling: immediate jittered retry per Retry-After header, otherwise exponential backoff.

I'll add concrete code and sample configs after this message.

--
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
Attachment referenced: redwood-sdk-samples.tar.gz

Monica
